note: Decision records (roadmap step 3) for the demo, so the graph shows a conflict being classified and decided. The conflicts are real: they come from the Microsoft Fluent Android Community file (exported 2026-10-11) and the Fluent 2 iOS kit (2026-10-12). The iOS kit gains a Danger button, and Transparent neutral stays an iOS-only button. The call and the deciders are the demo's placeholder owners, not a real Fluent team's. Replace them with your own team's call, or add one with `civic decide`.

decisions.title: Update the Android kit with an Outlined button
decisions.rationale: The Android kit predates Fluent Android's Compose controls and draws only Primary and Text buttons. Compose ships OutlinedButton for Brand outline, and the contract keeps it, so Design adds an Outlined button to the kit. Until it lands, Android designers take Brand outline from the contract, not the kit.
decisions.revisitTrigger: The kit gains an Outlined button, or Compose drops OutlinedButton.

decisions.title: Add a Danger button to the iOS kit
decisions.rationale: Fluent iOS ships Danger for destructive actions, and the contract keeps it, so Design adds a Danger button to the iOS kit. A destructive action needs a designed look, not one improvised per product. Until it lands, iOS designers take Danger from the contract, not the kit.

decisions.title: Keep Transparent neutral as an iOS-only button
decisions.rationale: Transparent neutral is iOS's borderless bar button, a platform convention with no counterpart on web or Android. It stays an iOS-only variant, built from the iOS component rather than drawn in the shared kit.
decisions.revisitTrigger: Another platform adds Transparent neutral, or the iOS kit starts drawing it.
